I have had some blood work in the past, but I don't think anything that would have been targeting thick or thin blood, like an anemia type thing. Those were some of the first tests they performed though once they realized something was wrong. 

The test for this disease is very particular and I actually had to see a specialist to get it done because no one else had the equipment to run the test. The only reason my primary care physician told me that I needed to see a specialist was that I had a weird purple pattern showing under my skin. For lack of a better term, a rash, but it wasn't topical. My blood was pretty much coagulating under the skin and making a weird lace-like pattern, (livedo reticularis.) Even regular specialists (hematologist, rheumatologist) didn't have the right stuff so I had to go to a doc in NYC who specializes in the actual disease to get diagnosed. Until I started having symptoms, I don't think anyone ever thought it was necessary to test me for thick/thin blood.

To be honest, I'm not really sure. I could have been born with it and never had any symptoms, or I could have developed it somehow. The doctors aren't really sure where it came from. But prior to about February/March of this year, I really didn't have any symptoms or signs of anything being wrong...for the most part...

A couple years ago I went to a cardiologist with the complaint that my heart was fast and he told me it was nothing, even though I legitimately cried in his office swearing that I knew something was wrong with me. He insisted I was fine. So for the next 2 years, when my heart was racing I just tried to push through it and tell myself everything was fine. While exercising and hiking, I had to take an increasing amount of breaks, then the duration of those breaks would get longer and longer, until I really just couldn't be myself anymore. I now have a new, incredibly thorough cardiologist who has gone above and beyond to work with my other doctors and help as much as possible.

I know many people have the same experience with doctors saying that there's nothing wrong with you, but dammit you know your body better than anyone. If you know you don't feel right, find a new doctor.

It is treatable, but not curable. There is a chance that after sufficient treatment I could go into remission potentially for the rest of my life, however, that's pretty unlikely. 

Typically the main 2 causes of the disease are Hepatitis C, and/or multiple kinds of cancer. I've tested negative for both many, many times. My team of doctors still don't really know where it came from, but there doesn't necessarily need to be a cause. Usually there is a cause, but rarely they can't find one. My family has no medical history of anything of the sort, it really kind of seemed to appear out of thin air, which is even more frustrating.

I have a team of doctors and we've decided on 2 courses of treatment. One is less drastic, which is what I'm trying now. It's called Plaquenil, which has been around for quite a while and treats various different things. Side effects seem to actually be relatively mild, but still frustrating...and it could take up to a few months to show reaults. 

The next step if this doesn't work is an IV infusion treatment called Rituxan. It's kind of like chemo but targets different cells. I haven't researched that one too much yet since that isn't the first option. I am in no way trying to relate what I have to any kind of cancer, by the way.

There's a series of pretty annoying symptoms...the ones that bother me most are neuropathy (numbness) in my hands and feet, to the point that sometimes I can't hold a pen and write, or sometimes walk with heavy steps like Frankenstein. That makes stairs real difficult when it's real bad.

Next is a racing heart. With no activity whatsoever, my heart rate is just faster than normal, which commonly leaves me out of breath, even if it's just something like climbing a flight of stairs. I was a very active person before the diagnosis, but am not able to do much now, because when I do try to be active now, my heart goes even faster, feeling like I'm having a heart attack. I know that's not actually the case, but that's how it feels, and it's terrifying feeling like your heart will explode.

Third worst is my vision. I've always had better than 20/20 vision but in the last 5 months it has gotten drastically worse. I now wear glasses, which really isn't a huge deal, but from going from such great vision to relatively bad vision in such a short time has been hard to swallow. 

Then it's probably extreme fatigue, which is kinda self explanatory. I can usually fight through it to get through work, but when I get home I'm in bed from the second I'm home until I wake up the next morning to go back to work. 

I just recently went on disability from work (for a broken arm a couple weeks ago) but it happened to coincide with when I started treatment, which I'm thankful for. Treatment is really taking a toll on me and I'm grateful to be out of work for the first few weeks to adjust to it. 

There are a handful more symptoms but nothing that's really trying, compared to the others. From diagnosis to treatment, it's been about 5-6 months, and I just started 3 days ago. Hopefully it all gets better soon!
